name: Scrapfly Cloud Browser

modes.label: Discovery overage
modes.note: 120 credits/hour. Hard quota cap, no overflow. Unspecified guest OS is not a selectable OS guarantee.

modes.label: Pro overage
modes.note: 120 credits/hour. Overflow $0.00035/credit; allocation minimum 5 credits across time + traffic, NOT additive start fee. Unspecified guest OS is not a selectable OS guarantee.

modes.label: Startup overage
modes.note: 120 credits/hour. Overflow $0.0002/credit; allocation minimum 5 credits across time + traffic, NOT additive start fee. Unspecified guest OS is not a selectable OS guarantee.

modes.label: Enterprise overage
modes.note: 120 credits/hour. Overflow $0.00012/credit; allocation minimum 5 credits across time + traffic, NOT additive start fee. Unspecified guest OS is not a selectable OS guarantee.

plans.name: Discovery
plans.note: 200,000 shared credits/month; no overage Browser traffic 7 datacenter/52 residential credits/MB.

plans.name: Pro
plans.note: 1,000,000 shared credits/month; extra $3.5/10 k, batches of 10 k. Included USD is overage-equivalent valuation. Browser traffic 10 datacenter/78 residential credits/MB.

plans.name: Startup
plans.note: 2,500,000 shared credits/month; extra $2.0/10 k, batches of 10 k. Included USD is overage-equivalent valuation. Browser traffic 8 datacenter/65 residential credits/MB.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: 5,500,000 shared credits/month; extra $1.2/10 k, batches of 10 k. Included USD is overage-equivalent valuation. Browser traffic 8 datacenter/65 residential credits/MB.

plans.name: Custom
plans.note: Custom: '$1,200 to $30,000+' monthly base, credits/extra/concurrency negotiated; 'Yes, above 5.5M credits per month'. HIPAA/BAA only on Custom.

features.ip_note: Datacenter pool by default ($1.08/GB Discovery), residential pool $7.99/GB Discovery down to $6.05/GB Enterprise, plus managed Tor; no mobile or BYO proxy documented.

caveats: Storage, snapshot GiB-month and public IPv4 prices are not published in the reviewed sources; null is not free.

No guaranteed vCPU allocation published; browser-hour is not a verified 4-vCPU/8-GiB VM equivalent. The sizes card keeps unknown hardware null; do not coerce it to zero or auto-rank against resource-guaranteed VMs.
Browser RAM is not published unless a specific mode overrides it.
Very low prepaid effective hourly rate excludes bandwidth. Do not use fee/credits as overflow rate: published overage is higher.
Cloud Browser docs explicitly define GB=1024 MB, unlike default estimator GB≈GiB simplification. MB rounds up; VNC/RTC add-ons and CAPTCHA consume the same quota.

5-credit allocation minimum applies to combined time + traffic, not five extra credits on every session. It cannot be exactly represented by card start_fee. Card uses null rather than inventing a time-only minimum.
Credit overflow is purchased in 10 k blocks; engine continuous arithmetic needs ceiling correction. Discovery stops at quota. Free grant 1,000 credits once, not $1,000.
Session resume (auto_close=false) keeps the browser running and billing after disconnect; there is no free paused state.

Pay-as-you-go overflow is automatic on Pro+, but 'Some accounts require a balance to consume Pay As You Go usage' and are rejected with HTTP 429 when the prepaid balance does not cover it. Discovery/Pro/Startup are suspended immediately on failed payment (Enterprise 7-day, Custom 30-day grace).
Unused plan credits do not roll over.

Cloud Browser /unblock endpoint (anti-bot pre-bypassed session, residential only): the billing calculator applies UNBLOCK_SURCHARGE = 1.2 to the residential credits/MB rate (e.g. Pro 78 -> 94 credits/MB). Sessions 'are billed until explicitly closed or they reach the browser_timeout limit' (max 1800 s).

fleet.verification: No card for free key, but official KYC policy applies to ALL customers: company name/address/activity, phone, email, planned use/experience; automated identity checks and manual use-case review. Further information can be requested.
fleet.tiers: Discovery 5, Pro 20, Startup 50, Enterprise 100; Custom committed concurrency.
fleet.notes: New signup includes 1,000 free credits but inspected pricing does not state its concurrency; paid Discovery 5 is not presumed trial default. 10 Pro, 50 Startup, 300/1,000 Custom. Request concurrency not generic machines. KYC page says most signups activate in minutes; that is not a quota increase SLA.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: After a Cloud Browser run stops, its full profile (cookies, storage, tokens, fingerprint, proxy identity) is saved to storage.
snapshot_auto.note: Browser product. On a clean stop of a named session the browser profile (cookies, local/sessionStorage, trust tokens, fingerprint, proxy identity; no tabs or live JS state) is saved automatically, but it is documented only as a one-way handoff into the Web Scraping API (session=cb:<id>), not restored into a new Cloud Browser session. Session resume (auto_close=false) just keeps the live browser running and billing until timeout (max 30 min); after termination reconnect fails ('Session expired or was terminated'). So no automatic save/restore of the browser machine on the next start.

harness_api.quote: takes a plain-English task description, plans the scraping steps, executes them using Scrapfly tools, and returns structured results
harness_api.note: `scrapfly agent` is a client-side CLI agent loop using your own LLM key (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY etc.) that calls browser tools; it does not run inside the cloud browser and there is no API to drive an agent harness inside the session. Browser Use / Stagehand / Vercel agent-browser integrations run on the customer's side and connect over CDP; the optional in-browser MCP endpoint (enable_mcp) exposes browser tools, not a harness.

ingress_rules.quote: Comma-separated list of IPs or CIDRs trusted to attach without a password.
ingress_rules.note: Applies to the live-control endpoints of a session (VNC/RTC human-in-the-loop): off unless enable_vnc etc. is set, attach requires a user-chosen session password, optional hitl_allowed_networks IP/CIDR list. CDP WebSocket requires the API key. There are no arbitrary exposed service ports in this product.

guest_firewall.note: Managed Chromium (Scrapium) sessions accessed only over CDP/WebSocket (plus optional VNC); no shell/root in the browser host, so no in-guest nftables/iptables. Not stated explicitly in docs; follows from the product model.

secret_proxy.quote: Your code passes a vault name and a key on the connection URL. It never sees the password itself.
secret_proxy.note: Related but different: the Credential Vault (rolling out gradually; optional 1Password mirror) autofills login passwords/TOTP into the browser's password store server-side and redacts them from screenshots, DOM, VNC and Runtime.evaluate results, so the controlling script/agent never sees them. It is form autofill inside the browser (the secret does enter the browser process), not a proxy injecting credentials into outbound HTTP requests; API-credential 'blob' items are never injected into the browser. No HTTP header/credential injection proxy documented.

image_oci.quote: Cloud Browser provides remote browser sessions accessible via WebSocket using the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP).
image_oci.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - Cloud Browser only launches its own managed Scrapium/Chromium browser; there is no way to boot a machine from a customer-supplied Docker/OCI image.

docker_inside.quote: Cloud Browser provides remote browser sessions accessible via WebSocket using the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP).
docker_inside.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - customers get a remote browser via CDP, not shell/root access to run their own containers.

nested_virt.quote: Cloud Browser provides remote browser sessions accessible via WebSocket using the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP).
nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - there is no guest OS/shell exposed to customers, so no /dev/kvm access.

desktop.quote: Take live control of a Cloud Browser session with your mouse and keyboard using any VNC client.
desktop.note: Live VNC control of the browser session (human-in-the-loop) is offered, scoped to the browser window rather than a full OS desktop.

ssh.quote: Cloud Browser provides remote browser sessions accessible via WebSocket using the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP).
ssh.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - access is via CDP WebSocket (and optional VNC for the browser UI), not SSH to a machine.

snapshot.quote: auto_close=false ... Prevents the browser from being terminated when you disconnect.
snapshot.note: There is no filesystem or memory snapshot/restore of the browser machine; 'session resume' just keeps the same live browser process running (still billed) so you can reconnect. Once a session is actually terminated it cannot be restored ('Session expired or was terminated').

snapshot_on_demand.quote: All browser state including cookies, localStorage, sessionStorage, and navigation history is preserved across connections.
snapshot_on_demand.note: No API/CLI call exists to take an explicit snapshot/checkpoint of a session; state carry-over only happens via the live 'auto_close=false' resumable session or the one-way handoff of the saved profile into the Web Scraping API.

fork.quote: Cloud Browser provides remote browser sessions accessible via WebSocket using the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP).
fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - there is no API to clone a browser session/machine into new ones; each session/proxy identity is allocated fresh or resumed by ID, not forked.

fork_running.quote: Cloud Browser provides remote browser sessions accessible via WebSocket using the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP).
fork_running.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - no cloning capability of any kind is documented.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Cloud Browser provides remote browser sessions accessible via WebSocket using the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP).
memory_snapshot_fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - no fork feature exists at all, so memory-preserving forks are not offered.

pause_resume.quote: Session resume (auto_close=false) keeps the browser running and billing after disconnect; there is no free paused state.
pause_resume.note: Disconnecting with auto_close=false keeps the browser fully live (and billed) rather than pausing it; there is no mechanism to pause a session so billing stops/reduces and later resume it.

wake_on_request.quote: If you omit auto_close=false (defaults to true), the browser terminates the moment your script disconnects.
wake_on_request.note: A session is either kept alive (billed) via auto_close=false or is terminated on disconnect; a terminated session does not auto-wake on a new request under the same id - a fresh session is created instead.

persistent_disk.quote: Cloud Browser provides remote browser sessions accessible via WebSocket using the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP).
persistent_disk.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - there is no general-purpose filesystem exposed to customers; only browser profile data (cookies/local storage/fingerprint) carries over via session resume or the Web Scraping API handoff, not an arbitrary persistent disk.

volume_attach.quote: Cloud Browser provides remote browser sessions accessible via WebSocket using the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP).
volume_attach.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - no volumes concept exists for a managed browser-only product.

volume_shared.quote: Cloud Browser provides remote browser sessions accessible via WebSocket using the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP).
volume_shared.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - no volumes at all, so no shared-volume mounting across machines.

auto_stop_idle.quote: timeout | No | 900 | Maximum session duration in seconds (15 minutes default, 30 minutes max).
auto_stop_idle.note: Every session has a hard timeout (default 15 min, max 30 min) after which it is automatically stopped; auto_close also terminates the browser as soon as the client disconnects unless overridden.

live_resize.quote: Cloud Browser provides remote browser sessions accessible via WebSocket using the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP).
live_resize.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - there is no customer-controlled CPU/RAM sizing for a browser session, so nothing to resize live.

agent_harnesses.quote: takes a plain-English task description, plans the scraping steps, executes them using Scrapfly tools, and returns structured results
agent_harnesses.note: The `scrapfly agent` CLI runs client-side (using your own LLM API key) and calls Scrapfly's browser tools; no coding-agent harness (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, etc.) is preinstalled or offered as a template inside the Cloud Browser sandbox itself.

own_agent_api.quote: scrapfly agent ... takes a plain-English task description, plans the scraping steps, executes them using Scrapfly tools, and returns structured results
own_agent_api.note: Agent Mode is a local CLI loop against the customer's own LLM key, not a first-party hosted API endpoint that runs Scrapfly's own browser/research agent server-side; no such hosted agent API is documented.

lang_python.quote: Scrapfly Web Scraping API | Python SDK
lang_python.note: First-party Python SDK (scrapfly-sdk) is published and documented for driving the Scrape/Cloud Browser APIs.

lang_node.quote: Typescript SDK is the easiest way to access Scrapfly API in Typescript, Javascript and NodeJS.
lang_node.note: First-party TypeScript/JavaScript SDK supports Node.js, Deno, and Bun.

public_ipv4.quote: Datacenter pool by default ($1.08/GB Discovery), residential pool $7.99/GB Discovery down to $6.05/GB Enterprise, plus managed Tor
public_ipv4.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - customers reach the managed browser only via a wss:// CDP endpoint; outbound egress uses shared datacenter/residential proxy pools, and there is no dedicated public IPv4 assigned per machine.

inbound_https.quote: Cloud Browser provides remote browser sessions accessible via WebSocket using the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP).
inbound_https.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - the browser is reached only via wss:// CDP (and VNC for HITL); there is no concept of exposing arbitrary customer service ports over HTTPS.

egress_allowlist.quote: proxy_pool | No | datacenter | Proxy network type: datacenter or residential
egress_allowlist.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - customers choose a proxy pool/country for outbound scraping traffic, but there is no provider-side outbound allow/deny list or no-internet mode documented, since the whole point of the product is unrestricted web access through the browser.

egress_http_rules.quote: block_images / block_styles / block_fonts / block_media / blacklist ... Stub known analytics, tracking, and telemetry URLs.
egress_http_rules.note: Available controls are client-side content stubbing (images/styles/fonts/media/known trackers) to save bandwidth, not provider-side egress rules enforced at the HTTP method/path level for security purposes.

static_egress_ip.quote: Datacenter pool by default ($1.08/GB Discovery), residential pool $7.99/GB Discovery down to $6.05/GB Enterprise, plus managed Tor; no mobile or BYO proxy documented.
static_egress_ip.note: Outbound IP comes from shared datacenter/residential proxy pools selected per-session (optionally pinned to a country); no dedicated fixed outbound IP per customer/machine is documented.

gpu.quote: Cloud Browser provides remote browser sessions accessible via WebSocket using the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP).
gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - this is a managed headless/headed browser product with no GPU compute instances offered.

windows.quote: os | No | random desktop | Operating system fingerprint: linux, windows, or macos
windows.note: 'windows' here only selects a browser fingerprint (OS persona reported to the target site); the underlying Cloud Browser host is not an actual customer-usable Windows machine, so there is no real Windows machine offering.

macos.quote: os | No | random desktop | Operating system fingerprint: linux, windows, or macos
macos.note: Same as windows: 'macos' is only a fingerprint persona for the emulated browser, not a real macOS machine offered to customers.

self_host.quote: Scrapfly is a managed web scraping and browser automation platform.
self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - Scrapfly is delivered only as a hosted SaaS API/product; there is no distributable package to run the Cloud Browser stack on customer infrastructure.

byoc.quote: Scrapfly is a managed web scraping and browser automation platform.
byoc.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - no deployment-into-customer-cloud-account option is documented; it is a single shared managed SaaS.

open_source.quote: Scrapfly is a managed web scraping and browser automation platform.
open_source.note: The core Cloud Browser/Scrapium/Scrape API product is closed-source and commercial; Scrapfly only publishes client SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go, Rust, Scrapy) as open source on GitHub, not the service itself.

arm64.quote: os | No | random desktop | Operating system fingerprint: linux, windows, or macos
arm64.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - Cloud Browser session parameters only let you pick an emulated OS/device *fingerprint* (linux/windows/macos, or a mobile persona); there is no parameter to choose or verify an underlying machine architecture (x86_64 vs arm64), so no ARM machine is offered to customers.

sso.quote: Workspace owners can require all members to have two-factor authentication enabled.
sso.note: The Workspace & Team docs describe dashboard login via email/password plus optional org-enforced 2FA and per-domain invite restrictions; no SAML/OIDC single sign-on integration is mentioned there or on the compliance/trust pages, which otherwise enumerate security controls (RBAC, MFA, audit trails) in detail. Absence across the dedicated team/security documentation is treated as a considered 'not offered' rather than a gap.

eu_data_residency.quote: GDPR SCCs & UK ADDENDUM · ON REQUEST EU General Data Protection Regulation. Standard DPA applies to every account. Personalized SCCs (EU Module 2 / Module ...
eu_data_residency.note: Scrapfly relies on Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs Module 2) for international data transfers rather than offering an EU-only processing/storage region; no docs page or pricing/region selector lets a customer pin Cloud Browser sessions or account data to EU infrastructure, so residency is handled via transfer safeguards, not in-region-only storage.
